claims.text: Al in the X site of CrFeCoNiX promotes formation of a continuous protective oxide above 900 °C.
The protective oxide formed by Al-containing CrFeCoNiX is primarily Al2O3.
The oxide scale on Al-containing CrFeCoNiX grows slowly and remains coherent.
The scale on Al-containing CrFeCoNiX is more resistant to cracking and spallation than scales on corresponding Si- or Mn-containing alloys.
A coherent, adherent Al2O3 scale limits oxygen diffusion into the underlying alloy.
Alloying CrFeCoNiX with Al increases the availability of Al at the alloy surface.
The presence of Cr facilitates selective oxidation of Al into a dense and adherent Al2O3 layer.
The Al2O3 layer acts as a barrier to oxygen and corrosive species.
Blocking oxygen and corrosive species reduces further oxidation.
Reduced oxidation prevents stresses that would otherwise cause oxide cracking or spallation.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn predominantly form less protective or less coherent oxide scales than CrFeCoNiAl.
After prolonged high-temperature exposure, Al-containing alloys will show lower weight gain, fewer cracks, and more uniform oxide layers than Si- or Mn-containing controls.
The proposed behavior applies to both single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
The proposed behavior applies in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres at temperatures of 900 °C and above.
Phase distribution and localized diffusion behavior may affect oxide growth rate and cracking behavior.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis specifies temperatures above 900 °C, which excludes exactly 900 °C, whereas the conditions and boundary use ≥900 °C and the proposed experiment permits exposure at 900 °C.
